digest: This case, initially flagged as a critical ransomware attack, has been identified as a scheduled and approved detection validation exercise (CHG-4821) conducted in an isolated cyber-range. No actual malicious activity, data compromise, or impact to production systems occurred.

evidence_findings.title: Approved Simulation Activity
evidence_findings.subject: Detection Validation Exercise
evidence_findings.evidence: Case comments and artifact notes explicitly state this is a scheduled quarterly detection-validation exercise (CHG-4821) approved by the SOC lead, occurring within the isolated BUILD-LAB network.
evidence_findings.conclusion: The reported activity is an authorized and planned simulation.

evidence_findings.title: Isolated Environment
evidence_findings.subject: Network Isolation
evidence_findings.evidence: CMDB identifies `BUILD-LAB-03` and `SIM-CONTROLLER-01` as isolated cyber-range assets with no route to production. Firewall logs confirm all external egress was blocked during the exercise.
evidence_findings.conclusion: The simulated activity was contained within an isolated lab environment, posing no risk to production systems.

evidence_findings.title: Simulated Malware Execution
evidence_findings.subject: Process Execution
evidence_findings.evidence: The process `attack-simulator.exe` was executed on `BUILD-LAB-03` by `svc_detection_test` with the command line `--scenario ransomware-safe --no-encryption`. EDR recorded only simulation markers, confirming no actual file encryption, credential access, persistence, or payload download occurred.
evidence_findings.conclusion: The reported malware execution was a controlled simulation, not an actual compromise.

evidence_findings.title: Benign C2 Traffic
evidence_findings.subject: Network Communication
evidence_findings.evidence: Simulated C2 beacon traffic was observed from `10.250.0.23` to the internal exercise controller `10.250.0.10` on port 8443, confirming it was contained within the isolated lab.
evidence_findings.conclusion: The C2 beacon traffic was part of the simulation and did not involve external malicious infrastructure.

evidence_findings.title: Validated Simulation Tool
evidence_findings.subject: Binary Integrity
evidence_findings.evidence: The binary hash of `attack-simulator.exe` matches the internally signed validation tool inventory.
evidence_findings.conclusion: The executable used for the simulation is a known and approved tool.

attack_chain.description: The `attack-simulator.exe` was executed on `BUILD-LAB-03` by the `svc_detection_test` account as part of the approved exercise.
Simulated C2 beacon traffic was observed from `10.250.0.23` to the internal exercise controller `SIM-CONTROLLER-01` (`10.250.0.10`).

attack_timeline.attack_behavior: Case created, marking the start of the approved simulation window.
Analyst `analyst_mrivera` added a comment confirming the activity as a scheduled detection-validation exercise (CHG-4821).

ioc_indicators.context: Approved change request for the exercise

remediations.description: Close the case as a benign, approved activity, as no actual threat or compromise occurred.
Document the successful detection and validation of the exercise, noting the findings for future reference.
